newsitem.title: USA: Stock market regroups; merger-dominated trading.
newsitem.headline: Stock market regroups; merger-dominated trading.

text.p: The stock market regrouped Tuesday after last week's rally through the 7,000-point level in the Dow Jones industrial average, and investors turned their attention to a burst of merger activity.
At 1 p.m. EST, the 30-stock blue-chip Dow was up 6.92 points at 6,995.88.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on volume of 259 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was off 4.75 points at 1,362.44, and the American Stock Exchange index was up 2.06 at 596.21.

"We're seeing consolidation after the big move. The focus has shifted to mergers and acquisitions, which are dominating the tape today while the rest of the market takes a breather," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist for Oppenheimer & Co.
The Dow drew strength from a rally in stock of Philip Morris Cos., which was up 3-1/4 at 128-3/4.

"The mergers are symptomatic of a slow-growth environment in which it is hard to get top-line earnings growth so you get it from hollowing out the middle," Metz said. "They allow restructuring to reduce expenses and improve earnings. They help the overall market because speculators search around for possible next targets and bid them up."
Great Western Financial Corp. was up 9-3/8 at 43-5/8, topping the NYSE most active list, after H.F. Ahmanson & Co. said it was offering $42.53 a share for Great Western. Ahmanson rose 3-3/4 to 44-14.
Renaissance Hotel Group N.V. jumped 4-1/2 to 29-5/8 after Marriott International Inc. said it agreed to acquire Renaissance for $30 a share cash in a deal worth $1 billion.
Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp. was up 2-3/8 at 16-5/8 and Healthsouth Corp. lost 1-3/4 to 41-3/8 on news of their $1.6 billion merger.
But analysts said that aside from the interest in mergers, traders were likely to take it easy and wait for Wednesday's January consumer price index to give them some guidance.

"I have the impression that traders and portfolio managers are shaking out the cobwebs after the long weekend," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. "We've all had a chance to see where we are and have reached the conclusion that we have come awfully far awfully fast."
He said the stock market, as measured by the Dow, had risen 8.4 percent from the start of the year through Friday, having closed above 7,000 points on Thursday.
"The chances of keeping this up are not good," Johnson said. "Investors have decided to pull in the reins and slow down a little bit."

The rally in shares of Philip Morris came after the company said that a West Virginia judge had dismissed the "essential claims" of the state attorney general's Medicaid reimbursement lawsuit against tobacco companies.
